title: The Ass and the Load of Salt
summary: A merchant bought several sacks of salt at the coastal saltpans, loaded them onto the back of his donkey, and set off toward the market town. The day was sweltering, and the donkey...
keywords: the ass and the load of salt
full_text:
A merchant bought several sacks of salt at the coastal saltpans, loaded them onto the back of his donkey, and set off toward the market town. The day was sweltering, and the donkey groaned beneath the heavy, abrasive burden.

While crossing a shallow river, the donkey stumbled over a slippery boulder and plunged into a deep pool. By the time the merchant helped the beast back to his feet, a large portion of the salt had dissolved into the cool water, making the sacks remarkably light! The donkey trotted on to the town with brisk joy, delighted by his good fortune.

A few days later, the merchant returned to the coast for another load of salt. Remembering the pleasant river crossing, the cunning donkey deliberately stumbled and threw himself into the water at the same ford. Once again, the salt melted away, and the donkey walked free of his heavy burden, braying in smug triumph.

The wise merchant saw through the animal's deceit and resolved to teach him a lasting lesson. On their third trip, instead of salt, the merchant packed the panniers full of dried sponges and raw wool.

Reaching the river, the foolish donkey smiled to himself and plunged intentionally into the deepest pool, waiting for the burden to melt away. But the dry sponges and dense wool soaked up gallons of water like thirsting sand! When the donkey tried to rise, the load had tripled in weight, crushing him down into the riverbed.

He had to stagger up the steep, muddy riverbank carrying a mountainous burden of waterlogged weight, learning that a trick played once too often becomes its own punishment.
moral: Tricks devised to shirk duty often turn back upon the trickster with double weight.
